doc.title: Jack Sheldon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Future of jazz and struggling to improve
summary: He is optimistic about jazz and still working to improve.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: What’s the future of jazz look like for you?
I figured out, if I keep improving at the rate that I am now, I don’t quite have enough time to get good, but I’m working at it though.
I’ll bet if you move a few numbers around in your formula, I’ll bet you can get good.

Well I’m so limited, I mean I’m working at stuff now, I’m working on my tonguing and I want to get stuff. Well you know, you’re a player, you really can never get it as good as I want it. There are certain nights where I’m real good and everything seems to work, but most of the time it’s a real struggle. Do you find it that way?
I guess so. Sometimes you’re your own worst critic.
